text:
Noah Hanifin's season is easy to summarise: 6 points in 18 games, 20 minutes a night, 32 blocked shots, and almost nothing unusual in the numbers. His finishing is on schedule, the luck around him is neutral, and Vegas takes 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five.

The one flag is relative: the Golden Knights are about 3.5 points better in that share without him. Some of that is likely deployment on a team where Shea Theodore drives the offense. He played 24 minutes against both New Jersey and Boston last week, so Vegas leans on him when it's tight.

His best moment lately was a pass. The Athletic's Jesse Granger called it a "great pass by Hanifin" that set up Trevor Connelly's bank-shot equalizer in Pittsburgh on Nov. 3. Evolving-Hockey had him 63rd among 215 defensemen last season, mostly from even-strength defense, and he skates well (90th percentile burst speed). He's 29, the fifth pick in 2015 between Mitch Marner and Pavel Zacha. We project about 30 points. Steady is the job, and he's doing it.
headline: Hanifin is doing the steady work
